exposure: induction using prostaglandins (prostaglandin E1 or prostaglandin E2)
induction using nonprostaglandin methods (oxytocin, amniotomy, mechanical dilation)
outcome: cesarean deliveries for nonreassuring fetal heart tracings
cohort: The study included term, singleton, nonanomalous pregnancies with fetal growth restriction (estimated fetal weight <10th percentile for gestational age) who underwent induction of labor, excluding those with previous cesarean deliveries.
finding: There were no differences in adverse neonatal outcomes between prostaglandin and nonprostaglandin induction methods, but prostaglandin use was associated with higher rates of cesarean delivery and cesarean delivery for nonreassuring fetal heart tracings.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean delivery was higher in inductions using prostaglandins compared to those using nonprostaglandin methods.
birth_weight: estimated fetal weight <10th percentile for gestational age (fetal growth restriction)
